assay: recA-defective mutant rec30; double-strand break repair after gamma irradiation
finding: rec30 repairs very few or no double-strand breaks after 1.75 Mrad and is markedly radiosensitive

assay: recA point mutants recA670 (rec30) and recA424; gamma survival
finding: rec30 is extremely radiation sensitive; recA424 (recombination-defective, co-protease active) only slightly, implicating co-protease activity in resistance

assay: lexA deletion and non-cleavable LexA; gamma survival and DSB repair kinetics
finding: neither lexA deletion nor non-cleavable LexA changed survival or double-strand break repair kinetics after gamma irradiation
loss of pprA function accounts for the loss of radiation resistance of mutant KH311
PprA binds broken double-stranded DNA and stimulates end-joining by ATP- and NAD-dependent DNA ligases
deleting pprA reduces UV survival up to eightfold; profound UV sensitivity combined with ddrA or ddrD deletion

assay: pprA deletion; DSB repair kinetics and cell division after gamma irradiation
finding: delta-pprA repairs double-strand breaks efficiently (about 1 h delay) and is not needed for RecA-independent repair; radiosensitivity is attributed to defective DNA segregation/cell division, not repair

assay: ddrA (DR0423) deletion; ionizing radiation survival and genome reassembly
finding: deletion increases sensitivity to ionizing radiation; without nutrients the mutant fails to reassemble its genome
deletion of ddrA increases mitomycin C sensitivity about 100-fold

assay: ddrB/recA double mutant; DNA fragment rejoining (PFGE) after irradiation
finding: DNA fragment rejoining is severely compromised in the ddrB/recA double mutant, implicating DdrB in RecA-independent repair
inactivating ddrB increases mitomycin C sensitivity
recN null mutant shows substantial sensitivity to various DNA-damaging agents

assay: dr1819 (uvsE) disruption in uvrA-1 background; UV survival
finding: interrupting dr1819 greatly sensitizes a uvrA-1 strain to UV, consistent with an alternative excision repair pathway
